comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Root cause proven; fix pushed as Gerrit change 2337

**Mechanism (confirmed, not inferred).** Sign and verify resolve the op-cert key from two
different places:

- SIGN: `ensure_opcert_key` (`_opcert_signing.py:155-206`) takes the context-local startup
  binding first. `compose_startup_opcert_binding` (`mcp_server.py:717-746`) composes it from
  `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY`, and `run_mcp` binds it around the whole
  serving loop (`_mcp_health.py:325-329`), so every tool call — sign AND verify — runs inside it.
- VERIFY: `_opcert_own_public_key` (`:238-258`) consulted neither the binding nor
  `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`; it read `<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub` and self-healed only from
  `<tracker>/.opcert-key`.

Live read-only probe of the deployed container (`rebar-mcp-afe01efaa8b2-8092`,
i-00880b2c7f13527c5) on 2026-08-28:

```
REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH=UNSET      REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY=SET
REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID=SET          REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY=UNSET
/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets/: .env-id only — no .opcert-key, no .opcert-key.pub
/run/secrets/: opcert-ed25519-key (0600, private half only)
```

The tracker has NO `.opcert-key` even though the server signs successfully. That is the proof
the binding is observed on the sign path: unbound and override-less, the first
`ensure_opcert_key(create_if_missing=True)` would have generated one there.

**Gerrit change 2328 (`seaborne-wisdomless-songbird`) does not fix this.** Its premise — "the
ContextVar binding is not observed on every tool-call path, so no step yields a key" — is
refuted by the two facts above. `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` is read only by the SIGN-side
`ensure_opcert_key`, which the bound server never falls through to, and the failing VERIFY-side
reader never consults it. Setting it is a no-op for this failure: neither necessary (signing
already works) nor sufficient (verification still returns `foreign_key`). A regression test
here (`test_key_path_override_cert_certifies_in_the_same_environment`) reproduces exactly
2328's config and is RED without the code fix. Recommend abandoning 2328.

**Fix (change 2337).** Verification resolves the public half from the same ordered chain the
signing side resolves the private half (binding → `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` → tracker genesis),
deriving the public line in-process with `ssh-keygen -y` and taking every key the environment
holds as the trust root. `_derive_opcert_pub` now returns the derived text as well as caching
it, because a bind-mounted secret's directory is read-only and the cache can never be written
there. No deploy change, no new secret.

**Mutation-checked.** With the fix reverted, 3 of the 4 tests fail with the exact production
reason ("this environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature"); with
it, all 4 pass. The 4th (tracker genesis) passes both ways and is the regression oracle.

Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `tests/unit/test_module_size_contract.py`,
`check_complexity_baseline.py --check` (new=0 increased=0) all pass; 1017 opcert/signing/attest
tests pass.

**Scope.** AC1-AC4 of the revised plan are addressed. AC5 (warn at mint when the environment
cannot verify its own signature) and AC6 (deploy health check) remain open follow-ups; with
this fix the key-path divergence that produced the silent uncertifiable cert is no longer
reachable, but neither guard exists yet. AC1's on-box demonstration needs 2337 deployed.

Related but distinct: `gold-distinct-lacewing` (eca3) is the `.env-id` re-identification bug
(principal mismatch); this one is the absent public key. Different verdict, different mechanism.

comments.body:
## Verified against the merged fix; closing

**Merge SHA: `83edf9972728ae1e0729a39098ec70e4fab4617a`** — Gerrit change 2337, "Verify op-certs
with the key that signed them". Confirmed an ancestor of `origin/main` and of the worktree HEAD
used for this close. It touches exactly two files (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`,
`tests/unit/test_opcert_own_pub_resolution_d26a.py`) — no deploy, infra, or secret material.

### AC1 — live sign-then-verify on the DEPLOYED server: `certified` [non-codebase]
Not a re-read of a pre-existing attestation: a FRESH manifest carrying a one-time nonce was
signed on the deployed server and then that exact certificate was verified.

```
sign_manifest   c67b-ece5-707e-460e   manifest[0] = "probe-d26a-f437916502b3: AC1 round-trip
                                                    probe for bug d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a"
                                      nonce: f437916502b3   signed_at 1787958784894243861
  -> algorithm sshsig, principal 9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65

verify_signature c67b-ece5-707e-460e --kind probe-d26a-f437916502b3
  -> verified: true, verdict: "certified"
     reason: ssh-keygen -Y verify accepted signature for principal
             '9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65'
     signed_manifest == the nonce-bearing manifest just signed
```

The probe subject is `ruby-griffinish-goitered` (already closed obsolete, disposable) and the
manifest's leading token minted an ISOLATED attestation kind slot, so its `plan-review` and
`completion-verifier` attestations were untouched. The original reproduction in this ticket's
description ran on the same server under the same principal `9f1c8e42-…` and returned
`foreign_key` / "this environment has no op-cert public key"; the same round trip now certifies.

### AC2 — one resolution chain for both halves
`_opcert_own_public_key` is gone; its successors are `_opcert_own_key_paths` +
`_read_opcert_pub` + `_opcert_own_public_keys` (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`).
`_opcert_own_key_paths` appends, in order, `_current_binding().key_path`, then
`os.environ["REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH"]`, then `opcert_key_path(tracker)` — element-for-element the
order `ensure_opcert_key` uses on the write side. `_read_opcert_pub` prefers the cached `.pub`
and otherwise derives in-process via `_derive_opcert_pub` (`ssh-keygen -y -f <key>`).
`verify_opcert_record` now builds its trust root from `_opcert_own_public_keys(tracker)`.
No key material was added to the deployment: the commit changes no infra file.

### AC3 — derivation never needs a write beside the private key
`_derive_opcert_pub` now RETURNS the derived text; the `<key>.pub` cache write is wrapped in its
own `try/except OSError` that logs, unlinks the temp file, and falls through to
`return proc.stdout…strip()`. So a read-only key directory yields the public line anyway.
Pinned by `test_certifies_when_the_key_dir_is_read_only`, which chmods the secrets dir to 0500
and asserts both `verdict == "certified"` and that no `.pub` was created there.

### AC4 — tracker-genesis path unchanged
`_ensure_opcert_pub`, `_generate_opcert_key` and `ensure_opcert_key` are untouched by the diff:
genesis still writes the `.pub` cache, and `create_if_missing=False` still refuses to create a
key on the verify side. `test_tracker_genesis_still_certifies_and_caches_its_pub` asserts the
cache write; the other three tests assert `<tracker>/.opcert-key` is never created by verifying.

### AC5 / AC6 — split out, not silently dropped
Filed as `879b-9bf0-86fd-4a6b` (`weaponless-textile-cutworm`), linked `discovered_from` this
bug: the mint-time WARNING when no public counterpart resolves, and the deploy/startup health
check. Both are additive guards against the class regressing rather than part of this
key-resolution fix. No pre-existing follow-up covered them (searched before filing).

### DD1 — RED before, GREEN after (re-verified independently, not taken on trust)
Post-fix (worktree at `origin/main`, which contains 83edf997): 4 passed.
Pre-fix: a second worktree detached at `83edf9972728^` with the post-fix test file copied in and
`PYTHONPATH` pinned to the PRE-FIX `src` (confirmed via `rebar.__file__` and the ABSENCE of
`_opcert_own_public_keys`) gives **3 failed, 1 passed**, each failure carrying the exact
production reason "this environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature".
The one that passes both ways is `test_tracker_genesis_still_certifies_and_caches_its_pub` — the
AC4 regression oracle, which is supposed to be invariant. My first attempt at this check ran the
post-fix package under a symlinked venv and vacuously passed 4/4; that run was discarded.

### DD2
Satisfied by the AC1 round trip above, run after 2337 was deployed. [non-codebase]

### Scope note
Only the "this environment has no op-cert public key" branch of `foreign_key` was the defect.
The other branch — refusing a certificate whose principal names a DIFFERENT environment — is
documented intended behaviour (ADR 0104) and was deliberately left alone; nothing here was
ticked on the basis that cross-environment certificates should verify.

Closing `close_class=regression` against `--ref 83edf9972728ae1e0729a39098ec70e4fab4617a`.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Correction to the close-class named at the end of the previous comment: closing
`--class plan_defect`, not `regression`.

Reasoning against the bounded vocabulary in `docs/ticket-model.md`:

- `plan_defect` ("the design/plan itself was wrong") — CHOSEN. The op-cert key-custody design
  gave the SIGN side three resolution sources (bound startup signer, `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`,
  tracker genesis) but specified only ONE for the VERIFY side (`<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub`).
  The two halves were never designed to share a chain, which is precisely what 2337 corrected.
- `regression` — REJECTED: it means a change reintroduced a previously-FIXED defect. This
  mismatch was never fixed before; it was latent from the moment the write side gained
  resolution branches the read side did not mirror.
- `env_integration` — REJECTED: the deployment (a read-only bind-mounted secret, a tracker with
  no keypair) only EXPOSED the defect. The fault and the fix are both in rebar's own code
  (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py`), so this is not an environment or integration issue.
- `preexisting` — REJECTED as less precise: the defect was indeed latent, but naming it
  `plan_defect` records WHY it was latent, which is the useful signal for the follow-up
  `879b-9bf0-86fd-4a6b` guards.

```
rebar transition d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a in_progress closed \
  --class plan_defect --ref 83edf9972728ae1e0729a39098ec70e4fab4617a
  -> transitioned d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a: in_progress -> closed; unblocked: none   (exit 0)

rebar verify-signature d26a-8ffa-97cd-4b2a --kind completion-verifier
  -> SIGNATURE[completion-verifier]: certified — ssh-keygen -Y verify accepted
     signature for principal 'b8a354e0-12c3-4cf2-bbf1-fcc9685d5126'
```

Attestation manifest carries `completion-verifier: PASS` and
`verified-at-sha:83edf9972728ae1e0729a39098ec70e4fab4617a` — the close verified the pinned
immutable merge SHA, not a moving `origin/main` (bug `rookie-fickle-hydra`).

The close gate also required a current plan-review attestation
(`require_plan_review_for_close = true`); the prior one was `stale-code` because the fix itself
changed both `file_impact` dependencies. A fresh `rebar review-plan --ref 83edf997…` returned
PASS with 0 blocking / 1 advisory and signed at the same pinned SHA, after which
`review-plan --status` reported `certified`. No `--force` and no gate override was used at any
point.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The deployed MCP server mints op-cert signatures it can never verify. Every attestation it
produces — the plan-review cert at claim and the completion-verifier cert at close — is
permanently uncertifiable on the same box, so `claim` through the deployed server is refused
for every ticket.

Observed 2026-08-27 against the LIVE MCP server (`https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp`),
signing and then immediately verifying on the same server:

```
sign_manifest {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered", "manifest": ["probe: ..."]}
  -> {"algorithm": "sshsig", "key_id": "9f1c8e42-...", "envelope": "{...}"}   # SUCCEEDS

verify_signature {"ticket_id": "ruby-griffinish-goitered"}
  -> {"verified": false, "verdict": "foreign_key",
      "reason": "this environment has no op-cert public key; it cannot certify any signature"}
```

`claim_gate_check` (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py:113-133`) reads a non-`verified`
result as "no certified plan-review attestation" and denies the claim. That is the P1.

## Mechanism — sign and verify resolve the key from two DIFFERENT places
This is a path mismatch, not a missing file. The signing and verifying halves do not share a
key-resolution chain.

SIGN side — `ensure_opcert_key` (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:155-206`) resolves, in order:
the context-local startup binding's process-owned key copy; else `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`; else
the `<tracker>/.opcert-key` genesis. The deployed server takes the FIRST branch:
`compose_startup_opcert_binding` (`src/rebar/mcp_server.py:717-746`) composes a signer from
`REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` + `REBAR_IDENTITY_SIGNING_KEY` (`/run/secrets/opcert-ed25519-key`), and
`run_mcp` binds it around the serving loop (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py:325-329`), so every tool
call signs under a process-owned copy of the MOUNTED key.

VERIFY side — `_opcert_own_public_key` (`src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:238-258`) consults NEITHER
the binding NOR `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`. It reads `<tracker>/.opcert-key.pub`, and its
self-healing branch re-derives that `.pub` only from `<tracker>/.opcert-key`. On this box the
tracker holds NEITHER file (verified in-container: only `.env-id` and `.ensure-applied`), so the
self-heal cannot fire and the function returns `None`. `verify_opcert_record`
(`:528-535`) then answers `foreign_key`.

The tracker re-clone (`7be0edb7132d`) is context, not the cause: even with a tracker-local
keypair present, it would be a DIFFERENT keypair from the mounted signing key, so verification
would still fail (as `mismatch` rather than `foreign_key`). Regenerating tracker-local key
material is therefore NOT a fix.

`REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH` is likewise not a fix: it is read only by the SIGN-side
`ensure_opcert_key`, which the bound server does not even reach, and the verify-side reader
never consults it.

## Impact
rebar mints exactly two op-cert kinds (ADR 0049). On this server both are
signed-but-uncertifiable: the claim gate refuses every ticket, and a close records a
`completion_signature` that `verify_signature` cannot certify. A project that later enables
`verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since` would find every attestation this
server produced rejected. Signing succeeds while verification is structurally impossible, so
nothing surfaces the problem when the certificate is minted.

## Reproduction
1. Against the deployed MCP server, call `sign_manifest` on any ticket with a one-item manifest.
2. Observe it succeeds and returns an `sshsig` envelope.
3. Call `verify_signature` on the same ticket.
4. Observe `verdict: "foreign_key"`, reason "this environment has no op-cert public key".

## Fix
Make the verify side resolve the public half from the SAME ordered chain the sign side resolves
the private half (binding, then `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`, then tracker genesis), deriving the
public line in-process from the resolved private key with `ssh-keygen -y`. Deriving — rather
than shipping a second secret — is required because the deployment key is bind-mounted
READ-ONLY, so no `.pub` cache can be written beside it; the derived text, not a file, is the
authority. No new secret, mount, or deploy change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] [non-codebase] AC1: On the deployed MCP server, a `sign_manifest` immediately followed by `verify_signature` on the same ticket returns `verdict: "certified"`, `verified: true`.
      provenance: environment=deployed rebar MCP server https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp (box i-00880b2c7f13527c5); principal=9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the defect exists only in the deployed server's own key-resolution environment, so the proof is a live sign-then-verify round trip on that server, which no repository fact can supply.
- [x] AC2: `_opcert_own_public_key`'s successor resolves the public key from the same ordered
  chain as `ensure_opcert_key` — bound startup signer, then `REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH`, then
  `<tracker>/.opcert-key` — deriving the public line in-process from the resolved private key.
  The deployment ships no additional key material.
- [x] AC3: Deriving the public line never requires writing beside the private key: a key whose
  directory is read-only (the bind-mounted secret) still certifies.
- [x] AC4: The unbound tracker-genesis path is unchanged, including its `.pub` cache write, and
  verification still never creates a private key.

AC5 and AC6 (the deferred mint-time WARNING and the deploy/startup health check) are SPLIT OUT
to `879b-9bf0-86fd-4a6b` (`weaponless-textile-cutworm`), linked `discovered_from` this bug. They
are additive guards against the class regressing, not part of this key-resolution fix, and are
out of scope here.

## Definition of Done
- [x] DD1: AC2, AC3 and AC4 covered by a regression test that is RED before the fix and GREEN
  after it — `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_own_pub_resolution_d26a.py`.
- [x] [non-codebase] DD2: AC1 demonstrated against the deployed MCP server after the change is deployed.
      provenance: environment=deployed rebar MCP server https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/mcp (box i-00880b2c7f13527c5); principal=9f1c8e42-7a3b-4d5e-b6c1-2f0a9d8e7c65; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — a post-deploy demonstration is an outside-world event on the running server, not a repository fact.

file_impact.reason: resolve the op-cert public key from the same chain that resolves the signing key (bound signer, REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH, tracker genesis)
regression test: sign-then-verify certifies under a bound signer, under a key-path override, and on a read-only secrets mount
